speaker: thabo_mokoena
headline: THE GAP BETWEEN POLICY AND LIFE HAS A CLASS ADDRESS.
deck: When institutions report progress but households still absorb the same costs, the gap itself becomes part of the political economy.
quote: A programme can exist on paper while the worker still pays for the failure with wages, time and debt.
facts: Formal access does not guarantee usable access.
Delayed relief is often financed by household debt.
Unpaid time is part of the real cost of administration.

gaps.reality: Travel, queues and documentation still cost money.
Payment delay shifts the waiting cost to the household.
Workers still absorb the risk when delivery breaks.

takeaway: The structural gap is not empty space; it is where public failure becomes private cost.
